scope: Lionfish Watch. Question: where should we prioritise lionfish surveys, given recent sightings, reef heat stress and ocean conditions? Lionfish (Pterois volitans/miles) only, in four areas: Florida Keys (fl-keys), Mexican Caribbean (mx-caribbean), Belize (belize, thin) and Colombian Caribbean (co-caribbean, thin). Sightings are not abundance; heat stress is context; no single risk percent; field conditions stay separate from priority.

newTools.name: reef_heat
newTools.purpose: NOAA Coral Reef Watch values (CRW_SST, CRW_SSTANOMALY, CRW_DHW, CRW_BAA) at reef cells of the four areas, latest or as a daily series, with the data date and latency.
newTools.input: { area?: 'fl-keys' | 'mx-caribbean' | 'belize' | 'co-caribbean', bbox?: BBox, from?: RFC 3339, to?: RFC 3339, at?: RFC 3339 }
newTools.output: rows of { area, cell, lat, lon, date, sstC, anomalyC, dhwCWeeks, baa, baaLabel, latencyDays, series?: [...] }

newTools.name: marine_forecast
newTools.purpose: Open-Meteo Marine hourly forecast (wave height, wave period, current velocity converted from km/h, current direction) for an area point or place, 72 hour horizon, with daily summaries and the model run time.
newTools.input: { area?: string, place?: string, lat?: number, lon?: number, days?: number (max 3) }
newTools.output: { point, runAt, horizonHours, hourly: [{ at, waveM, wavePeriodS, currentKmh, currentMs, currentDirDeg }], daily: [{ date, waveMaxM, waveMeanM, currentMaxKmh }] }

newTools.name: source_info
newTools.purpose: Static facts about one feed of the active app: publisher, API URL, human page, licence and attribution text, cadence, typical latency, rate limit, coverage limits, and what the feed can and cannot tell us. Read from the app config, no network call.
newTools.input: { feed: string (a feed id of the active app, e.g. usgs, nwps, crw) } or {} for all feeds
newTools.output: rows of { feed, publisher, apiUrl, pageUrl, licence, attribution, cadence, latency, rateLimit, coverage, limits[] }

newTools.name: evidence
newTools.purpose: Fetch one cited record by evidence id (wraps GraphQL `evidence(id)`): the record, its source API URL, publisher page, fetch time, ingest lag, feed state and links such as duplicateOf or the forecast issuance it belongs to.
newTools.input: { id: string (C14 evidence id, e.g. reading:..., sighting:..., forecast:...) }
newTools.output: { id, kind, record, sourceUrl, sourcePageUrl, fetchedAt, ingestLagSeconds, feed, links[] }

newTools.name: team_board
newTools.purpose: Read the active app's team board (GraphQL `board(id: "<app>:main")`): missions with their sites or areas and dates, and committed messages with author, recipient, thread and time. Human records, not a data feed.
newTools.input: { kind?: 'missions' | 'messages' | 'all', about?: string (place, site or area name), hours?: number (default 168) }
newTools.output: { missions: [{ id, title, place, bbox, start, end, assignees }], messages: [{ id, from, to, thread, at, body }] }

toolChanges.change: Resolve the four area ids and names and places inside them (Cozumel, Banco Chinchorro, Glover's Reef, Turneffe, San Andrés, Looe Key, Key Largo); refuse places outside the four areas with their names.

Add `dateField: 'observed' | 'submitted'` and `knownAt` (ingested at or before); rows carry submittedAt, lag days, positional accuracy or obscured flag, and duplicateOf for GBIF copies of iNaturalist (matched on catalogNumber) so duplicates are never counted as corroboration.
For lionfish, rank areas and cells by the L5 priority heuristic and return the four components (recent reports, ID quality, heat stress, completeness) separately; no single risk percent.
Terms are the four lionfish components with value, weight and rationale, plus evidence ids for the supporting reports and CRW cell.
Compare buoy (NDBC, CO-OPS) water temperature with GOES-19 and CRW SST in Florida, and say no buoy exists in the other areas.

changelog.change: lionfish-change-previous-month and lionfish-boundary-population: the forbid patterns matched the honest negation the pass phrases ask for ("does not mean the population grew", "cannot say whether the population is growing"); a lookbehind now exempts negated forms. lionfish-quality-buoy-vs-satellite: expectedTools geocode dropped; the question spans all four areas, so one conditions call over the app is the honest answer and geocoding one area would narrow it.

population forbids: the negated form still matched when a possessive sat between the negation and the noun ("whether Belize's lionfish population is growing"); the lookbehind now exempts a negation word anywhere earlier in the sentence (2 patterns).
lionfish-replay-90d-mx: the span phrase accepted only "90 days"; "90-day record" and "three-month" name the same span, so the pattern now takes either spelling (1 pattern).

J1 (gates/leaf-J1.md): pass.phrases (regexes) migrated to pass.mustSay: every regex phrase became a plain-language statement judged by an independent model (apps/web/eval/judge.ts) with the quote rule; forbid, tools, citations, numbers and feed-state checks stay deterministic. Script: scripts/migrate-phrases-to-mustsay.ts.

J1 wording review after the first live run: statements that read as conjunctions or carried the intent rather than the regex were reworded to the regex's meaning after the first live run (docs/grading/judge-validation.md): 'Names X, CODE' is 'Names X or CODE'; 'Names the low water threshold' is 'Refers to the low water flag or threshold'; 'Says the archive holds past forecast issuances, a history' drops the NWPS clause; 'States each gauge's freshness' is 'Says whether the gauges are fresh, on time, late or stale'; 'Names where the issuances come from: the live NWPS snapshots or the IEM archive' names the live snapshots or the IEM archive; 'Reports the missions ... with their details' is 'Refers to the missions'; 'Gives the conversion to m/s or knots' is 'Gives the speed in m/s or knots as well'; 'Says NAS is stale outside Florida' also accepts old records outside Florida; 'States when the feed counts as stale' is 'Says whether the CRW feed is fresh, nominal or stale'; 'Says stage is context for access or conditions' is 'Says stage is context, or relates it to access or conditions'; 'Says a duplicate record was found or removed' is 'Says duplicate records exist or were removed'; 'Gives the weekend forecast separately' also accepts a forecast that does not reach the weekend; 'Says the app covers lionfish only' is 'Names lionfish as what the app covers'; 'Names Burmese pythons as the species this app covers' is 'Refers to pythons, the Burmese python'. Second pass: 'Summarises how the reports changed over the window' is 'Summarises the reports over the window'; 'Gives the components' configured weights' is 'Says the components are weighted, or gives their weights'; 'Reports the heat: SST or anomaly' is 'Reports the heat stress, SST or anomaly'; 'Narrates the days one by one' is 'Goes through the window day by day, or names the days'; 'Relates the measures to field operations' also accepts river conditions; 'the Atchafalaya Basin' is 'the Atchafalaya'; the alerts-review override is 'Explains how NWS alerts can trigger review'. Third pass, after the second live run: every remaining 'each site's', 'per site', 'with its …' or semicolon clause that the regex did not require was dropped or turned into an 'or' (26 statements), for example 'Names the sites that need review' for the regex 'review' is 'Refers to the review status or which sites need review', 'States the forecast error per site' is 'States the forecast error or difference'. 'Calls the NAS data stale, with its newest record date' is 'Says the NAS data is stale, old or not current' (the date alone, which the regex accepted, does not answer whether the data is current). After the final series: 'Places the scene in January 2026' is 'Places the scene in the January cold snap' (the regex was (January|2026-01)); 'Gives the quality flag' is 'Gives the quality flag, or notes cloud masking' (the regex accepted 'cloud'). After the held-out series: the outside-area refusal statement also accepts naming the eight locations as the coverage (the scope guard's wording); 'States NAS's lag of weeks to months' is 'Says NAS records lag or arrive late, by weeks to months'; 'Names the buoy, the in-situ measured reading' also accepts its absence (Belize has no buoy); 'Names USGS NAS as a source' is 'Names NAS or USGS NAS as a source'. No statement was loosened below its regex.
